title: Finite cohomological dimension permits unbounded acyclic-complex computation
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], let $\mathcal B$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], and let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be additive and left exact, with right derived functors $R^qF$ [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Suppose there is an integer $d\geq0$ such that $R^qF(M)=0$ for every $M\in\mathcal A$ and every $q>d$. Use cochain complexes, quasi-isomorphisms and derived categories as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Then the unbounded right derived functor $RF:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B)$ exists, with its natural comparison $\alpha_L:Q_{\mathcal B}(F(L^\bullet))\to RF(Q_{\mathcal A}L^\bullet)$. For every unbounded complex $L^\bullet$ whose terms are $F$-acyclic [def-sp-acyclic], meaning $R^qF(L^r)=0$ for all $r\in\mathbf Z$ and $q>0$, $\alpha_L$ is an isomorphism. In particular, these isomorphisms identify the derived images of maps of such complexes with the termwise images under $F$, by naturality of $\alpha$.

source.place: Tag 07K7, lemma-unbounded-right-derived, assertions (1)-(2); apply with n=d+1 and enough injectives in A

proof.text: By [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives], $\mathcal A$ has enough injectives. The vanishing theorem [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-injective-vanishing] makes every injective object $F$-acyclic. Fix the given bound $d$: no object has positive derived cohomology in degree greater than $d$. All applications of the long exact sequence below are therefore in an abelian category with enough injectives.

source.place: Tag 07K7, lemma-unbounded-right-derived, assumptions and initial paragraph

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-kinjective-degreewise-existence] to $\mathcal A$. Every complex $K$ has a quasi-isomorphism $u_K:K\to I(K)$ to a K-injective complex with injective terms. Termwise application of the additive $F$ induces a functor $F_h:K(\mathcal A)\to K(\mathcal B)$: a homotopy equation $v-w=dh+hd$ remains that equation after applying $F$. This functor preserves shifts and cone triangles: for a chain map $v:X\to Y$, the canonical biproduct isomorphisms $F(Y^r\oplus X^{r+1})\cong F(Y^r)\oplus F(X^{r+1})$ send its differential to $\begin{pmatrix}F(d_Y^r)&F(v^{r+1})\\0&-F(d_X^{r+1})\end{pmatrix}$. Indeed the four entries are obtained by composing with the biproduct inclusions and projections; functoriality and additivity preserve these composites, zero and the minus sign. These isomorphisms also preserve the cone inclusion and projection, and $F(-d_X)=-F(d_X)$ identifies the shifted complexes. Thus the image of each cone triangle is its corresponding cone triangle. Thus $Q_{\mathcal B}F_h$ is an exact functor to $D(\mathcal B)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] to obtain $RF$ and a natural comparison $\alpha$, invertible on every K-injective complex. Only the source category is required to be Grothendieck.

source.place: Tags 070K/070Y, lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies / lemma-K-injective-defined; alternative existence input to Tag 07K7

proof.text: Let $C$ be any acyclic complex all of whose terms are $F$-acyclic, and set $Z^r=\ker(d_C^r)$. Exactness of $C$ gives short exact sequences $0\to Z^r\to C^r\to Z^{r+1}\to0$ for every integer $r$. For $q>0$ their long exact sequences [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] have zero outer terms $R^qF(C^r)$ and $R^{q+1}F(C^r)$, giving $R^qF(Z^{r+1})\cong R^{q+1}F(Z^r)$. For fixed $r,q>0$, iterating backwards $d$ times gives $R^qF(Z^r)\cong R^{q+d}F(Z^{r-d})=0$. The iteration has base zero iterations (identity) and induction step the displayed isomorphism at index $r-j-1$ and degree $q+j$. When $d=0$ the asserted vanishing is directly the given global bound. This uses finitely many cycle sequences for each $r,q$, with no convergence claim about an infinite filtration.

source.place: Tag 07K7, lemma-unbounded-right-derived, preservation of quasi-isomorphisms; direct finite dimension-shifting argument in place of bounded truncations

proof.text: In degree zero, the same long exact sequence, together with $R^1F(Z^r)=0$ from Step 3, yields $0\to F(Z^r)\to F(C^r)\to F(Z^{r+1})\to0$. Here $R^0F=F$, and left exactness identifies $F(Z^r)$ with the kernel of $F(d_C^r)$. The previous differential factors as the epimorphism $F(C^{r-1})\to F(Z^r)$ followed by the monomorphism $F(Z^r)\to F(C^r)$. Consequently its image is this kernel and $H^r(F(C))=0$ for every $r$. Thus applying $F$ to any such exact complex produces an exact complex.

source.place: Tag 07K7, lemma-unbounded-right-derived, quasi-isomorphism claim; cycle sequence calculation

proof.text: Now take a quasi-isomorphism $v:L\to M$ between complexes of $F$-acyclic objects. Its cone $C(v)$ is acyclic by [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic]. Each cone term $M^r\oplus L^{r+1}$ is $F$-acyclic: apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] to the split short exact sequence $0\to M^r\to M^r\oplus L^{r+1}\to L^{r+1}\to0$; for every $q>0$ its two outside $R^qF$ terms vanish, so the middle one vanishes. Steps 3-4 make $F(C(v))$ acyclic. The cone matrix computation in Step 2 identifies it with $C(F(v))$. The cone criterion again, now in $\mathcal B$, proves that $F(v)$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 07K7, lemma-unbounded-right-derived, quasi-isomorphism claim; finite biproduct and cone argument

proof.text: For the stipulated complex $L$ use $u_L:L\to I(L)$ from Step 2. Its target has injective and hence $F$-acyclic terms by Step 1, so Step 5 makes $F(u_L)$ a quasi-isomorphism. Naturality of the comparison gives $RF(Q_{\mathcal A}u_L)\circ\alpha_L=\alpha_{I(L)}\circ Q_{\mathcal B}(F(u_L))$. The right-hand side is invertible: its first factor is invertible on K-injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] and its second factor by the localization definition. The left factor $RF(Q_{\mathcal A}u_L)$ is also invertible because $u_L$ is a quasi-isomorphism and functors preserve inverses. Hence $\alpha_L$ is invertible. This proves computation for every unbounded complex of $F$-acyclic objects.

source.place: Tag 07K7, lemma-unbounded-right-derived, assertions (1)-(2); comparison with K-injective replacement

proof.text: For any map $v:L\to M$ of complexes with $F$-acyclic terms, comparison naturality reads $RF(Q_{\mathcal A}v)\circ\alpha_L=\alpha_M\circ Q_{\mathcal B}(F(v))$. Inverting the comparison components from Step 6 gives $RF(Q_{\mathcal A}v)=\alpha_M\circ Q_{\mathcal B}(F(v))\circ\alpha_L^{-1}$. This is exactly the claimed identification on maps, with no quasi-isomorphism assumption on $v$.
